questions_and_answers.answer: Taxable Income vs. Pretax Financial Income The taxable income of a corporation and its pretax financial income often differ due to two main types of differences: Permanent Differences and Temporary Differences. Permanent Differences Permanent differences are discrepancies between the financial income reported by a corporation and its taxable income that will not reverse over time. These differences arise due to items that are either only included in taxable income or in financial income, but not in both. Item Permanent Difference Non-deductible expenses Yes Income that is not subject to tax Yes Expenses that are not tax deductible Yes Income that is exempt from tax Yes Temporary Differences Temporary differences are discrepancies between the financial income reported by a corporation and its taxable income that will reverse over time.
